answer: Each agent carries a cryptographic pulse of reputation that is minted like pigment on a shared ledger; to join it must post a bond of native token, the nectar that fuels its stake. Periodically neighboring agents sample the pulse and run a zero‑knowledge challenge proving the binder’s identity; a successful proof returns the nectar plus a share of slashed bonds from any node that fails the test. An attacker must therefore acquire enough nectar to back every fake identity and risk losing it each challenge, making a Sybil flood economically prohibitive.
